explanations.text:
The skill is the rulebook claude reads before it explains a code
file for you. Three loops run through it, and one step meets them all.

The everyday loop — one file, one abstraction:

    you: "how does server.py work?"
         claude looks at the kind of file and takes the shape
         the catalog gives it — the rail for a page with one run,
         the sections for a file of functions, the desk for a
         file that only hands your line on, the dialogue for a
         rulebook — and writes the abstraction for a reader who
         knows the subject, not the code
                                                          ([explain](2. Explain))
         every name in it is a pin to a real thing:
         a block of the file, an earlier abstraction,
         or another file of the project
                                                          ([anchors](1. Anchors))
         claude shows the text and stops.
    you: "map it"
         the tool checks the pins and adds one entry     ([map](3. Map))
         claude tells you what went in and what is still
         not covered                                     ([report](6. Report))
    you: "these words are mine, keep them"
         the entry goes in plain and flagged as yours, with no pin
         in it; the pins come later, with a retext that may change
         no character — the tool compares the words with the ones
         it holds; --verbatim on a retext is the road for new words
         of your own, or for the flag on an entry mapped before it
         existed                                    ([your own words](3. Map))
    you: paste a line back
         claude finds the abstraction it belongs to
                                      ([how you point](How the user points at things))
         and rewords it in place, or undoes the last one
                                            ([rewrite](4. Rewrite and rollback))
         a retext never takes a stale mark off — only the repair
         does, so the tool knows the mending happened
    you: "new file" at the top of the reader's file tree
         type a path from the root, folders and all; the empty
         file opens on "new abstraction", and the tree follows
         the files on disk from then on           ([the reader](1. Anchors))

The training loop — one file, two or three abstractions, your pick:

    you: human login <key>
         once per machine, so the store knows whose sessions these
         are; the sessions live in that store and never on your
         disk                                        ([the store](7. Train))
         each session also carries the id of the project, so a
         session belongs to one user and one project
         without the key the training refuses and says to log in
    you: human train --open
         the rows of a changed file you did not pick last time
         come along
         when the store does not answer, a retext or a sync that
         makes an open row follow warns and goes on; an undo that
         must check the open session refuses instead
         a new telling you ask for from the reader — a first one,
         a plainer one, or one over words you highlight — opens a
         session by itself when none is open
    you: "how does server.py work?"
         claude writes the versions and gives them to
         the tool, one call each, each with the name of
         the shape it follows                              ([train](7. Train))
           best         the shape the catalog says
           refinement   a changed file only: the map's own text, filled
                        by the tool; a new abstraction has none — the
                        tool refuses one and the feed shows two cards
           free         whatever helps you most
         every call answers with the slots that are filled and,
         on its own line, the ones still empty; claude writes the
         missing one before it reports to you
         versions for another block, another entry, or other
         highlighted words of the same file make a row of their own;
         the versions over highlighted words must not pin into the
         entry that holds those words, and after the close claude
         pins those words down into the new entry
    you: "the whole project this time"
         the same versions, over a copy of every file
    you: "rewrite the refinement"
         claude hands the same slot in again; the earlier text
         stays under a v1 v2 v3 picker, and the pick takes the latest
    you: open the reader: the open session lies over the page as a
         layer, one row per file, the versions as cards; swipe,
         pick one per row, say why if you want
         hide the layer, and a chip in the head bar with the counts
         brings it back; a new row brings it back on its own
    you: human train --close, or the "close training" button
         the tool first names every row that still misses a
         version, then maps every pick itself; a pick that rewords
         an entry the project map stands on leaves a note there
         a new abstraction with no pick takes best, or free when
         best is missing, so a telling you asked for from the
         reader always lands; a changed file with no pick waits
         for the next session, because its current text already
         stands in the map

The project loop — the whole project, not one file:

    you: "how does the project work?"
         claude reads the top entry of the project's own map and
         the front door of every file, then writes the telling of
         the whole — the shape is claude's to pick, and claude says
         which one it took                       ([the whole](8. The project))
         its names pin to a file, to one block of a file, and to a
         name inside a file's abstraction, so you walk down from
         the project to the file to the code
         claude shows the text and stops.
    you: "map it"
         the tool keeps it in a map of its own, apart from the maps
         of the files                         ([the project map](3. Map))
         claude tells you what went in, and which files no line
         of the telling reaches yet
                                            ([the same report](6. Report))

The step every loop meets — the code changed:

    you: "sync"
         the tool carries the pins to the new lines, and claude mends
         the words that went untrue and adds a sentence for each
         behaviour the change added, once per change
                                                ([sync](5. Sync after a change))
         your own words are mended like any other text, because the
         map must follow the code: the smallest edit, in your voice,
         a warning with the lines, the origin kept, and one command
         that puts your words back
         a plainer layer with no pin into the code is never a candidate;
         it takes the new fact one layer down, on your word
    you: "repair the ones that went stale"
         one note per changed parent waits on the dependent — a parent
         changed twice keeps its first old text — and one call reads
         them all, mends the dependent, and takes the whole list off;
         the project telling is repaired the same way, each note
         naming its file

What the skill is, in one line: claude abstracts, the tool maps,
and only the tool writes the maps            ([decompile](decompile)).
